where: Test 2 R&W M2 Hard q22 — Transitions
note: Adjudicated: the marked key B is correct and the agent's answer was wrong, so no key change. Written by hand because the gate correctly refused to ship the agent's explanation, which argued for a different answer.
whyCorrect: The first sentence names something the library did well — energy-efficient windows and solar panels. The second reports a drawback of doing it: construction cost nearly 20 percent above a traditional building. A benefit followed by its price is a contrast, and however is the transition that marks one.

whyWrong.A: In addition signals another item of the same kind, which would need the second sentence to name a further advantage. Higher cost is not another advantage.
whyWrong.C: For example would make the higher cost an instance of building with efficient windows and solar panels. A cost is a consequence of that choice, not a case of it.
whyWrong.D: Therefore is the closest wrong answer, because the panels really did cause the extra cost. But a causal transition presents the second sentence as the point the first was building toward, and here it works against it — the sentence is a concession, so the contrast is what the passage needs.

commonMistakes: Choosing Therefore because the relationship really is causal. Both a cause and a contrast are present; the transition has to match how the writer is using the sentence, not only how the facts connect.
tips: When a sentence reports the cost of something just praised, expect a contrast transition even if the cost was genuinely caused by it.

where: Test 27 R&W M2 Easy q17 — Boundaries (rewritten)
note: The original had two independent clauses either side of the blank, which made both 'membrane. It' and 'membrane, and it' correct. rewrite_questions.mjs recast it around an appositive. This explanation belongs to the rewritten item; the agent's line still describes the old one, which is why insert.mjs now refuses to overwrite a MANUAL row.
whyCorrect: What follows the blank — a carotenoid that sits in the archaeal cell membrane… — renames the pigment just named. That is an appositive, and a non-restrictive appositive is separated from the noun it renames by a comma.

whyWrong.B: With no punctuation the appositive runs into the noun, so the sentence reads as though the red came from something called a bacterioruberin a carotenoid. An appositive has to be marked off.
whyWrong.C: A semicolon needs a complete sentence on both sides. A carotenoid that sits in the archaeal cell membrane and stiffens it… has no main verb of its own — it is a noun phrase, not a sentence.
whyWrong.D: Adding and turns one thing into two, as if the red came from bacterioruberin plus some separate carotenoid. There is only one pigment here, and the phrase after the blank is another name for it.

commonMistakes: Reading the long phrase after the blank as a clause because it contains verbs. Sits and stiffens both belong to that, inside the relative clause — the phrase as a whole is still a noun.
tips: If the words after the blank rename the noun before it, you are looking at an appositive, and the question is only about how to fence it off.
